Germany coach Jürgen Klopp has confirmed that the Dortmund midfielder  Felix Nmecha will no longer perform the  “Crown for Jesus” goal celebration due to pressure from left-wing activists and the club.

Nmecha had done the gesture (miming taking a crown off his head and placing it on the ground while kneeling) after scoring both goals in Dortmund’s 2-1 win over Elversberg. 

It was linked to the “The King’s Return” campaign associated with the Christian footballers’ network Ballers in God.

Klopp said he confronted Nmecha about how the gesture was being interpreted (left-wing activists consider Ballers in God as a hate group due to its traditional views on gender, sexuality and marriage).

The Borussia Dortmund president Hans-Joachim Watzke had earlier told Nmecha to stop the celebration.

He announced this at a meeting of the club’s Fan- und Förderabteilung (fan and support department), which had criticized the gesture and the group for positions it saw as conflicting with the club’s values on diversity and tolerance.

The club also:
- Distanced itself from Ballers in God.
- Decided the group should no longer promote current BVB players on its channels.
- Indicated that legal steps would be considered if the group continues using BVB players for promotion.

What's happening at Starbase, Texas is truly incredible. 

Deep in south Texas, Musk and his team have pulled in some of the most brilliant people on Earth to make space travel as normal and boring as air travel. 

The energy there is just insane. It feels like a modern day Manhattan project, but built for peace not war. 

The building pictured below is the actual factory where they build Starship, like a car factory for spaceships. You probably wouldn't have guessed it, since it looks like a nice office building. Most factories are cold and industrial but Starfactory feels warm, clean, with design touches that make you feel like you're in Silicon Valley. 

There's something really special happening here. I envy everyone who gets to work here and live here. Most people never get a chance to devote themselves to something so meaningful, something that potentially bends the river of human history. It kind of feels like a college town, except everyone's building spaceships instead of going to class.

I've spoken with several industry experts about Nvidia after Jensen's resignation.

They taught me a lot, and one point they raised was whether senior and veteran engineers will actually stay at an Nvidia without Jensen.

Most of Nvidia's senior and veteran engineers have already reached financial freedom thanks to the surge in Nvidia's stock.

For many of them, the main reason they stayed was Jensen Huang's unmatched charisma. Now that he's gone, it wouldn't be strange if they left Nvidia tomorrow.

Industry insiders told me that OpenAI and Nvidia's competitors are probably already calling Nvidia's senior and veteran engineers like crazy. They said if you promise a senior engineer a team of their own, the whole team will move with them.

At first, I was disgusted with the New York Times for publishing this.
